Title: The TJX Companies Q2 Results: Earnings date set for August 19
Summary: The TJX Companies, Inc. (NYSE: TJX) is scheduled to release its second quarter Fiscal 2027 sales and earnings results on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, before 9:30 a.m. ET. CEO Ernie Herrman will host a conference call at 11:00 a.m. ET to discuss the results, operations, and business trends, with a webcast available on TJX.com and a replay accessible until August 25, 2026. This announcement provides investors with a timeline to evaluate the off-price retailer's performance amidst current consumer spending patterns.

Title: UNFI Signs on to U.S. Food Waste Pact
Summary: United Natural Foods Inc. (UNFI) has joined the U.S. Food Waste Pact, a national voluntary agreement aimed at reducing food waste across the supply chain, led by ReFED and the World Wildlife Fund. This move aligns with UNFI's goal of achieving zero waste to landfill by 2030, having already diverted 85% of its food waste last year. The pact brings together various stakeholders to develop data-driven solutions to combat the significant problem of food waste in the U.S., which accounts for 29% of all food and contributes to greenhouse gas emissions and water usage.

Title: How MP Materials (NYSE:MP) Connects to the Electrification Wave?
Summary: MP Materials (NYSE:MP) is gaining attention due to the rising demand for metals essential in electric vehicles, data centers, and power grids, linking the company directly to the broad electrification trend. The company produces rare earth materials used in high-performance magnets and is expanding into magnet production itself. Rare earth materials are crucial for electric motors, generators, and electronic devices, making them vital for advancing electrified transportation, computing, and power infrastructure.

Title: Etsy to Cut 220 Jobs, or 12% of Workforce, in Restructuring Push; Authorizes $2 Billion Buyback
Summary: Etsy is set to lay off 220 employees, representing 12% of its workforce, primarily in product and engineering, as part of a strategic restructuring effort aimed at improving coordination and speed rather than solely cutting costs. This announcement coincides with Etsy's second-quarter results, which showed sales exceeding estimates and an adjusted loss partly due to the Reverb divestiture. The company also authorized a new $2 billion stock buyback program, following recent divestitures of Depop and Reverb to focus on its core handmade marketplace amidst intense competition.

Title: Etsy laying off 12% of staff in bid to streamline business, position for growth
Summary: Etsy announced layoffs affecting 12% of its workforce, approximately 220 employees, primarily within its product and engineering teams. CEO Kruti Patel Goyal stated these cuts are not for cost savings but to streamline the organization for faster innovation and future growth in a competitive e-commerce market. Despite a net loss for the quarter due to discontinued operations, Etsy reported stronger-than-expected sales and raised its full-year guidance for gross merchandise sales.

Title: Duke Energy Progress reaches agreement with North Carolina Public Staff and other stakeholders to deliver a lower-cost path to power North Carolina's future
Summary: Duke Energy Progress has reached an agreement with the North Carolina Public Staff and other stakeholders, including the Carolina Industrial Group for Fair Utility Rates, Carolina Utility Customers Association, North Carolina Sustainable Energy Association, and Walmart. This agreement will reduce the proposed rate increase by more than half, resulting in an average annual increase of 3.4% over two years, while still enabling critical infrastructure investments. Additionally, Duke Energy shareholders will contribute $10 million to low-income bill assistance and weatherization programs.

Title: After indoor-farm wind-down, retailers seek Edible Garden fresh herbs
Summary: Edible Garden (EDBL) is experiencing a significant surge in demand for its fresh herbs and organic produce from national and regional retailers. This increase is largely due to consolidation within the controlled environment agriculture sector, including the shutdown of a major indoor farming operator. Edible Garden reported strong Q1 2026 revenue growth of approximately 22.9%, with cut herb sales up by about 45.9%, and has secured new or expanded programs with major retailers like Walmart, Target, and The Fresh Market.

Title: Why brands like Gap Inc. and Staples are inviting their employees to be creators
Summary: Brands like Gap Inc. and Staples are increasingly leveraging employee-generated content (EGC) by encouraging their employees to act as creators. This shift is driven by the authenticity EGC provides and its effectiveness in reaching new audiences, particularly Gen Z. Companies are implementing various strategies, from integrating employees into existing affiliate programs to building dedicated employee creator networks, recognizing the persuasive power of employees who genuinely know and use their products.

Title: Ibotta, Inc. Earnings Call Signals Network-Driven Growth
Summary: Ibotta, Inc. announced its Q2 earnings, highlighting a return to year-over-year revenue growth ahead of schedule, primarily driven by expanding third-party publisher partnerships and increased redemption activity. While facing challenges in direct-to-consumer and advertising segments, the company maintained solid profitability and cash generation. Ibotta provided forward-looking guidance projecting continued growth, emphasizing its strategic shift towards a partner-driven model.

Title: CoreCap Advisors LLC Boosts Stock Position in Walmart Inc. $WMT
Summary: CoreCap Advisors LLC significantly increased its stake in Walmart Inc. (WMT) by 38.5% in the second quarter, now owning 67,574 shares valued at $7.65 million. This comes as Walmart reported a 7.4% year-over-year revenue growth and met earnings expectations. Despite a "Moderate Buy" consensus from analysts, the stock faces valuation concerns due to its high P/E ratio and recent insider selling.

Title: eBay CEO Jamie Iannone’s new playbook embraces AI tools while blocking AI buyers
Summary: eBay CEO Jamie Iannone is navigating the AI landscape by encouraging sellers to use its in-house AI tools for listings while banning third-party autonomous AI shopping agents from its platform. This strategy aims to amplify commissions and enhance customer experience, as evidenced by a 15% revenue increase and 51% net income growth in the second quarter. The company also recently finalized a $1.4 billion acquisition of Depop, focusing on used and refurbished items to differentiate from larger e-commerce competitors.

Title: NewEdge Advisors LLC Has $357.81 Million Stake in Walmart Inc. $WMT
Summary: NewEdge Advisors LLC has reported a $357.81 million stake in Walmart Inc., despite reducing its holdings by 2.0% in the first quarter. Title: Walmart Stock And 2 Consumer Staples Picks For Rising Food And Fuel Costs
Summary: This article analyzes three consumer staples stocks—Lamb Weston Holdings (LW), Walmart (WMT), and Utz Brands (UTZ)—in the context of rising food and fuel costs. It explores how these companies are positioned to either benefit from or be pressured by inflation, considering their operational strengths, market positions, and financial metrics. The analysis provides insights into each company's ability to navigate cost pressures and sustain profitability.

Title: Walmart Earnings: Bull Put Spread Trade
Summary: This article suggests a bull put spread trade for Walmart (WMT) stock ahead of its earnings announcement on August 20th, due to high implied volatility. The strategy involves selling a $107-strike put and buying a $104-strike put, offering a potential 20.97% return with capped losses if WMT remains above $107. The author highlights the benefits of time decay and decreasing implied volatility post-earnings, while also cautioning about risks like significant price drops and early assignment.

Title: Niagen Bioscience Launches Tru Niagen on Walmart.com, Expanding Access and Diversifying Its E-commerce Marketplace Presence
Summary: Niagen Bioscience has launched its Tru Niagen supplement on Walmart.com, significantly broadening consumer access to its leading healthy-aging NAD+ product. This move diversifies Niagen Bioscience's e-commerce presence, leveraging Walmart's substantial digital reach and health and wellness market share. The initial offering includes 300 mg Tru Niagen in 30-count and 90-count bottles, with more products to follow, aiming to meet consumers where they shop.

Title: General Mills, Inc. (GIS) News, Articles, Events & Latest Updates
Summary: This article provides recent news and updates concerning General Mills (GIS), including its stock performance post-earnings, product recalls due to contamination concerns, and a new collaboration to accelerate regenerative agriculture. It also features analysis comparing General Mills with Conagra and highlights its challenges in a shifting market.

Title: ICEE Introduces First-Ever National ICEE Day on Aug. 18 with Free ICEEs at More Than 1,800 Locations Nationwide
Summary: ICEE is launching its first National ICEE Day on August 18th, offering free small ICEEs at over 1,800 participating locations nationwide, including Walmart Fuel, Krystal, Urban Air Adventure Park, AMC Theatres, and Regal Cinemas. This new annual tradition aims to celebrate nearly six decades of the frozen beverage and thank its fans. Customers can also enter a contest to win an At Home ICEE Machine by sharing their experience on social media.

Title: Walmart Tests Fulfillment Cart Changes After Child Hit in Store
Summary: Walmart is implementing new safety measures for its in-store fulfillment carts after a child was hit by one. The company is testing guidance that includes shipping new wheels to stores and advising staff to pull carts instead of pushing them to improve visibility and safety. These changes come amid ongoing discussions with OSHA regarding workplace safety.

Title: Walmart sued over alleged voiceprint collection from customer calls
Summary: Walmart is facing a proposed class action lawsuit in Illinois, accusing the retailer of secretly creating biometric voiceprints from customer phone calls without obtaining the consent required by the state's Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA). The lawsuit alleges that Walmart uses AI to extract vocal characteristics and build unique mathematical templates of callers' voices, and monitors speech for emotional tracking, without properly informing customers or getting written releases. The plaintiffs seek class certification, an injunction, destruction of improperly retained data, and damages for alleged BIPA violations.

Title: First Trust Advisors LP Raises Stock Holdings in Howard Hughes Holdings Inc. $HHH
Summary: First Trust Advisors LP significantly increased its stake in Howard Hughes Holdings Inc. by 44.5% in the first quarter, now holding 57,951 shares valued at $3.7 million. Despite this increase in institutional ownership, analyst sentiment remains largely negative, with a consensus "Sell" rating and a $79 price target, and one analyst recently downgraded the stock to "strong sell." Howard Hughes reported strong quarterly earnings, beating analyst estimates with an EPS of $2.68 and revenue up 330.2% year over year.

Title: Ingles Markets Reports Q3 Sales Growth Following Contentious Board Battle
Summary: Ingles Markets reported modest Q3 sales growth to $1.37 billion, despite a slight decrease in net income, following a contentious board election. The Southeast grocer showed stronger operational improvement over the first nine months of FY2026, with net sales reaching $4.05 billion and net income surging to $78.3 million. The company is also navigating rising operating expenses, activist investor pressure, and recovery efforts from Hurricane Helene.

Title: Marcus & Millichap Brokers $3.3M Sale of Retail Center in Metro Charlotte, North Carolina
Summary: Marcus & Millichap has brokered the sale of Village Shoppes, a 12,075-square-foot retail strip center in Indian Trail, North Carolina, for $3.3 million. The property, located near a Walmart Supercenter, was fully leased at the time of sale and was acquired by a fund-based private equity group from a West Coast partnership. Harrison Creason, Andrew Margulies, and Kyle Carpentier of Marcus & Millichap represented the seller.

Title: Prestige Consumer Healthcare (NYSE: PBH) expands with $1,045.0M wellness deal
Summary: Prestige Consumer Healthcare Inc. (NYSE: PBH) reported its Q1 2027 earnings, revealing a 6.5% increase in total revenues to $265.7 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, primarily driven by the $1,045.0 million acquisition of the OTC Wellness Business, including the Breathe Right brand. Despite revenue growth, net income decreased to $29.177 million from $47.466 million year-over-year, and gross profit fell by 3.0% due to acquisition-related costs and amortization. The company also detailed subsequent events, including the $150.0 million acquisition of LaCorium Health and the issuance of $400.0 million in new senior notes to redeem existing debt.

Title: O’Reilly Automotive, suppliers sharing tariff refund benefits
Summary: O’Reilly Automotive is sharing the benefits of refunds from now-invalidated tariffs with its suppliers, as its sourcing model primarily relies on suppliers as the importer of record. The auto parts retailer stated that direct tariff rebates are handled through cost of goods negotiations and aims to ensure both O'Reilly and its supplier partners benefit. This approach differs from other retailers like Amazon and Walmart, which plan to return funds to customers or cut prices, and Ford, which will use refunds for business divisions.

Title: Earnings Flash (GEN) Gen Digital Inc. Reports Q1 Revenue $1.34B, vs. FactSet Est of $1.31B
Summary: Gen Digital Inc. (GEN) reported its Q1 revenue at $1.34 billion, surpassing the FactSet estimate of $1.31 billion. The company also expects its Q2 revenue to be in the range of $1.32 billion to $1.35 billion, with adjusted EPS projected between $0.71 and $0.73. This news comes as the company also posted Q1 adjusted EPS of $0.71 per share, exceeding the FactSet estimate of $0.69.

Title: Niagen Bioscience launches Tru Niagen on Walmart.com
Summary: Niagen Bioscience has launched its Tru Niagen NAD+ supplement on Walmart.com, making its healthy-aging product more widely available. The initial offering includes 300 mg bottles, with more products to follow. Tru Niagen, which contains patented nicotinamide riboside, is backed by numerous human clinical studies and is cited as the top-selling NAD+ supplement in the U.S. e-commerce market.

Summary: Where Food Comes From (WFCF) reported slightly increased Q2 2026 revenue of $6.6 million and improved profitability, with gross margins rising to 40.6% due to cost efficiencies. Title: Castor's 2015-built Magic Starlight Joins a Joint Venture
Summary: Castor Maritime Inc. announced it has completed a joint venture to acquire, own, and operate the M/V Magic Starlight, a 2015-built Kamsarmax bulk carrier. Castor contributed the vessel in exchange for a 30% equity interest in the joint venture and $18.75 million in cash, expecting a net gain of approximately $2.9 million in Q3 2026. The transaction, which closed on August 6, 2026, leaves Castor's fleet at 11 vessels, including the one owned by the joint venture, with the acquisition financed partly by an $11.5 million sustainability-linked senior term loan.

Title: Walmart announces nationwide product recall after 1 injury reported
Summary: Walmart has announced a nationwide recall of 1.77 million attic stairway ladders sold on its website and at other major retailers. The recall, initiated by Louisville Ladder Inc., is due to spreader bolts breaking during use, which has caused a fall hazard and resulted in at least one injury involving neck, head, and back trauma. Consumers are urged to stop using the ladders immediately and can register for a free repair kit.

Title: Pistachio nut butter sold at Walmart recalled. What Texas shoppers need to know.
Summary: Botticelli Foods has issued a voluntary recall for its Bettergoods pistachio nut butter, sold at Walmart locations in 19 states, due to potential salmonella contamination. The recall was initiated after three jars tested positive for salmonella during a routine inspection. Texas is not affected by this recall, and no illnesses have been reported to date.

Title: Kroger must do more to prevent forced labor | Opinion
Summary: This opinion piece argues that Kroger should join the Fair Food Program to prevent forced labor in its produce supply chain. The author, a co-founder of the Coalition of Immokalee Workers, highlights multiple instances where Kroger has been linked to forced labor allegations and criticizes the company's reliance on ineffective social audits. The article emphasizes that proactive prevention through programs like the Fair Food Program is more effective than responding to abuses after they occur, citing competitors who have already adopted such measures.

Title: Walmart Resets Store Operations After Shopping Cart Risk
Summary: Walmart is adjusting its store operations regarding the large carts used by employees to fulfill online orders after reports of shoppers being struck. This change highlights the operational complexities arising from the retailer's rapidly growing e-commerce business and its emphasis on faster delivery. While these adjustments are not expected to significantly impact earnings, they underscore Walmart's strategy of using its physical stores as multifaceted fulfillment centers to compete with online retailers.

Title: Walmart sped past Costco and is now 'steamrolling' the US EV charging map
Summary: Walmart is rapidly expanding its electric-vehicle charging network, leveraging its vast real estate footprint to install high-speed chargers in its parking lots across the U.S. By June 2026, Walmart had installed approximately 46 public fast-charging stations with 380 cords at 326 stores, surpassing Costco and becoming one of the fastest-growing EV charging networks in the country. This expansion is crucial for increasing EV adoption, especially in rural and underserved areas, by making charging more accessible and affordable, with Walmart even offering lower prices for loyalty program members.

Title: Walmart updates Symbotic Inc. (SYM) stake to 39.9% of Class A shares
Summary: Walmart Inc. has reported an updated beneficial ownership of 76,350,823 shares of Symbotic Inc. Class A common stock on an as-converted basis, which represents 39.9% of Class A common stock. Title: Locally-made Cummins engine to hit market in 2027
Summary: Cummins Inc. plans to launch its new X15 engine in 2027, with limited production starting in January and full production by the fourth quarter. This launch follows EPA clarification on emissions warranty requirements, which is expected to ease the transition for manufacturers. The X15N is part of Cummins' fuel-agnostic 15-liter engine platform, designed to use lower carbon fuel types like hydrogen or biogas.

Summary: In 2026, the digital channel in retail is growing faster than physical stores, with e-commerce approaching 25% of total retail sales. Title: Zohran Mamdani Targets Walmart, Amazon, Target and Others Over 'Illegal' E-Bikes and E-Scooters: 'Too Many Lives Have Been Cut Short'
Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani has launched a crackdown on online retailers, including Walmart, Target, Wayfair, Temu, and Amazon, for allegedly selling illegal high-speed e-bikes and e-scooters. Title: 2,300 Walmart stores now using digital shelf labels for instant price updates
Summary: Walmart has implemented digital shelf labels (DSLs) in 2,300 of its U.S. stores, with plans for a chainwide expansion within the next year. These DSLs allow for instant price updates, maintain price consistency, and help associates quickly locate items for restocking or online order fulfillment. The technology is designed to streamline operations for employees and improve the shopping experience for customers without collecting personal data.

Title: 11 New Five Below Finds That Can Pass as Pottery Barn for Way Less
Summary: Five Below is offering a new range of home decor items that mimic the high-end aesthetic of Pottery Barn but at significantly lower prices. Summary: A $59 fire-pit promotion on Walmart's Marketplace highlights the company's e-commerce growth strategy, where third-party sellers manage inventory and shipping, allowing Walmart to earn referral fees. Title: Taylor Farms pulls jalapeño products sold at grocery stores
Source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
Summary: Taylor Farms has initiated a recall of over a dozen jalapeño-containing products sold in grocery stores across the U.S. This action is linked to an expanding Salmonella outbreak that has sickened 345 people in 27 states. The affected products include dips, salsas, and guacamole, and were distributed to major retailers like Walmart, Target, Whole Foods, Trader Joe's, and Kroger.

Title: Taylor Farms recalls salsa and guacamole from Walmart, Kroger over salmonella risk
Summary: Taylor Farms has issued a voluntary recall of prepared food items containing jalapeños, including salsas and guacamole, from major retailers like Walmart, Kroger, and Whole Foods due to potential salmonella contamination. This recall follows a notification from Coast Citrus Distributors regarding their fresh peppers. The CDC and FDA are investigating a salmonella outbreak that has sickened 345 people, and Taylor Farms is also facing scrutiny over a separate cyclosporiasis outbreak linked to its products from central Mexico.

Summary: Tanger (SKT) raised its full-year 2026 outlook after strong second-quarter performance, driven by increased funds from operations, same-center net operating income, and tenant sales. These closures follow court rulings blocking its merger with Albertsons and come as Kroger recently announced the acquisition of Giant Eagle supermarket. The company expects a modest financial benefit from these closures and will offer affected associates roles in other stores.

Title: Retail Earnings Preview: Home Depot, Lowe's, Target, TJX and Walmart

Home Depot and Lowe's are expected to show modest growth due to a soft housing market, while Target's turnaround will be under scrutiny. TJX and Walmart are anticipated to report solid results, benefiting from value-seeking shoppers and grocery dominance, respectively.

Title: Uber Partners With Zipline for Uber Eats Drone Deliveries
Summary: Uber Technologies Inc. and drone company Zipline have announced a strategic partnership to scale fast delivery services across the United States for Uber Eats. The collaboration aims to achieve 1 million drone deliveries per day by the end of 2029, with initial deployments expected to begin later this year in markets like Dallas and Houston. This initiative is supported by a strategic investment from Uber into Zipline and seeks to transform delivery by significantly reducing times, costs, and emissions.

Title: Kroger Health president Colleen Lindholz to keynote GLP-1 Shopper Summit
Summary: Colleen Lindholz, president of Kroger Health, will deliver the opening keynote at the inaugural GLP-1 Shopper Summit on November 12. Her keynote, "Reimagining Food as Health," will explore the intersection of food, nutrition, and healthcare, focusing on how retailers can facilitate healthier choices for consumers, especially with the growing adoption of GLP-1 medications. The summit will examine how these trends are reshaping shopper behavior and future growth strategies for retail and CPG industries.

Title: Sprouts Farmers Market Stock And 2 Consumer Staples Retailers Facing Budget Pressures

It details each company's operations, market position, and the unique challenges and opportunities they face, from Sprouts' focus on healthy foods to Grocery Outlet's extreme value model and Albertsons' major restructuring efforts. The piece highlights how these companies navigate changing consumer spending habits and economic headwinds.

Title: Safeway closes more stores in 2026 after failed Kroger merger
Summary: Safeway is closing additional stores in 2026 as its parent company, Albertsons, reassesses its retail footprint after the collapse of its $24.6 billion merger with Kroger. The closures reflect mounting pressure on Albertsons' core business, with declining identical grocery sales and a new restructuring initiative called ACI Edge. The company is centralizing merchandising decisions and consolidating divisions to improve efficiency and generate benefits.

Title: Solely Brings Clean Fruit Snacks to Walmart Stores Nationwide

Solely's offerings at Walmart include six items: three Fruit Jerky 5-packs and three Fruit Gummies 10-packs, all made with 1-2 organic fruit ingredients and no artificial additives.

Title: McDonald’s, Whirlpool CEOs flag the same concern on the economy
Summary: CEOs from McDonald's, Kraft Heinz, and Whirlpool are observing a significant financial strain on lower-income consumers, impacting their sales data. This trend is evidenced by consumers cutting back on spending, increased reliance on credit card debt, and reduced savings rates. The article suggests that while these are not recession figures, they indicate a struggling consumer base due to rising costs of food, housing, and energy since 2020.

Title: Synchrony Taps OpenAI to Let Shoppers Check Out With Store Cards Inside ChatGPT

This collaboration aims to integrate financing and payments directly into AI chatbots, addressing the "agentic commerce" gap where users are typically redirected to external websites for transactions. While the partnership holds significant potential for both companies, hurdles remain, including consumer trust in providing payment information to AI, the time needed for full integration of various card types, and the negotiation of transaction economics among all parties involved.

Title: Tomato bisque soup kit sold at Walmart stores recalled

Consumers are advised to dispose of the product or return it for a refund and to contact a healthcare provider if symptoms of listeriosis develop.

Title: Starwood team lends $672M for outdoor U.S. storage lots

Title: Costco Expands Uber Eats Delivery to 47 States
Summary: Costco and Uber Eats have announced a significant expansion of their partnership, bringing Costco delivery through Uber Eats to 47 states, up from 17. Nearly 600 Costco locations are now available for on-demand or scheduled delivery via the Uber Eats app, allowing members to order a wide range of items. This expansion aims to further boost Costco's already thriving digital business, which saw a 21.5% increase in digital comparable sales in its third-quarter earnings report.

Title: Amazon raises minimum hourly pay by $1 to $20 for US operations workers
Summary: Amazon is increasing the minimum hourly pay for its eligible full-time U.S. operations workers by $1, bringing it to $20. The company also introduced a new benefit, "Day 1 Financial," providing low-cost banking services through First Tech Federal Credit Union. With this raise and existing benefits, Amazon states the average total compensation for these workers will now exceed $32 per hour.

Title: Kroger pulls Red Bull from its grocery stores and gas stations
Summary: Kroger has stopped selling Red Bull at all its stores and gas stations nationwide due to a pricing dispute with the energy drink's supplier. The supermarket giant is taking a firm stance against Red Bull's proposed wholesale price increase, betting that customers will opt for alternative brands rather than leaving the store. This move is part of Kroger CEO Gregory Foran's broader strategy to prioritize value for customers and improve in-stock availability.

Title: Grocery staple sold in California stores recalled for listeria. What to know
Summary: A frozen pasta product, Bettergoods Authentic Italian Lemon Alfredo Fettuccine from Gias Foods, has been recalled due to potential Listeria monocytogenes contamination. The recalled product was sold at select Walmart stores in California and nationwide, carrying UPC No. 194346442706 and specific expiration dates. Consumers who purchased the pasta are advised to return it for a full refund, though no illnesses have been reported to date.

Title: Casey's General Stores: A $100+ Post-Earnings Sell-Off - Why I'm Not Buying Yet (CASY)
Summary: Casey's General Stores (CASY) experienced a significant post-earnings sell-off despite reporting a double-beat quarter, largely due to concerns over valuation and slowing growth. While the company exhibits strong fundamentals like EPS growth and margin expansion, declining free cash flow and a forward P/E still above historical averages and peers make the author cautious. The article reiterates a Hold rating, suggesting a more attractive entry point around 25x earnings due to potential macro headwinds impacting sales and margins.

Title: Dollar General CEO says even $100k earners shopping like bargain hunters (DG:NYSE)
Summary: Dollar General's CEO, Todd Vasos, notes that persistent inflation and high gas prices are forcing consumers across all income brackets, including those earning over $100,000, to become more budget-conscious. This trend is leading even higher-income earners to shop like bargain hunters. The CEO's comments highlight the broad impact of economic pressures on consumer behavior.

Title: Is the Amex Platinum Worth the Massive Annual Fee? Here's My Honest Answer
Summary: The American Express Platinum Card comes with an $895 annual fee, which can be daunting, but the article argues it can provide over $5,000 in first-year value, largely through a substantial welcome bonus and numerous annual credits. While not suitable for everyone, especially those who rarely travel or dislike managing perks, the card can be highly beneficial for frequent travelers willing to utilize its extensive benefits. The author details various credits for hotels, digital entertainment, CLEAR+, Uber, and airlines, suggesting that leveraging even a fraction of these can easily offset the annual cost.

Title: DoorDash, Uber expand Costco delivery partnership in U.S.
Summary: DoorDash and Uber are expanding their delivery partnerships with Costco across the U.S., intensifying competition with Instacart. DoorDash will now offer same-day service from all U.S. Costco warehouses, while Uber has broadened its coverage to 47 states. These expansions are part of Costco's strategy to enhance its e-commerce presence, attract younger online shoppers, and deepen customer loyalty through broader delivery access and faster fulfillment.

Title: ERAYAK Power Solution Group Inc. Maps U.S. Expansion, Hybrid Home Power Roadmap
Summary: ERAYAK Power Solution Group Inc. has announced its plans for U.S. expansion, including increased distribution across Amazon, Walmart, and DTC channels. The company is also outlining a roadmap to scale from portable power solutions to tri-fuel inverter generators and residential energy storage systems in the 30 kW class. This strategic move aims to target the higher-ticket residential backup market and differentiate its offerings through fuel flexibility and an ecosystem approach.

Title: Hour Loop Falls 22% in Three Months: Should You Buy the Dip or Wait?
Summary: Hour Loop (HOUR) shares have dropped 22% in the last three months, underperforming the industry and broader market, primarily due to heavy reliance on Amazon, rising fulfillment costs, and liquidity issues. Despite these challenges, the company is experiencing strong revenue growth, benefiting from a technology-enabled platform, and its stock is currently trading at a discount, suggesting a potential buying opportunity for investors.

Title: Walmart launches rural health ambassador pilot, tapping pharmacists for expanded support
Summary: Walmart is initiating a six-month pilot program where pharmacists in five rural stores will act as "Health Ambassadors." These ambassadors will help customers navigate health and wellness resources, focusing on areas like diabetes, weight management, and maternal health. The initiative aims to leverage Walmart's community presence to make health resources more accessible in underserved rural areas.

Title: Capri Sun teases new oversized, refillable pouch. How to get one
Summary: Capri Sun is releasing a limited-edition, refillable 24-fluid-ounce "Big Pouch" in response to strong fan demand for a larger size. The pouch will be sold exclusively on Walmart.com starting September 21st for $6, and its permanent inclusion in the product lineup will depend on customer feedback. This move follows other large-format releases by Kraft Heinz, indicating a trend towards bigger versions of their popular products.

Title: Walmart is accelerating its battle against Amazon with a weapon that the e-commerce giant cannot copy: more than 4,000 stores
Summary: Walmart is leveraging its extensive network of over 4,000 physical stores to compete with Amazon, transforming them into distribution and delivery centers for its rapidly growing e-commerce business. This strategy has resulted in a 23% increase in global e-commerce sales, with stores fulfilling a significant portion of online orders and accelerating delivery times. Walmart's approach integrates physical and digital operations, aiming to use its brick-and-mortar presence as a key advantage in the e-commerce landscape.

Title: Walmart Supercenter under construction in Liberty Hill
Summary: A new 176,000-square-foot Walmart Supercenter is under construction in Liberty Hill, Texas, and is expected to open in late 2027. This development is set to anchor a large retail complex at Santa Rita Ranch and could attract other businesses to the rapidly growing Austin area. The project highlights the ongoing retail expansion in the region's suburban communities.

Title: Kroger pulls Red Bull from shelves nationwide
Summary: Kroger has removed Red Bull from all of its stores and fuel centers nationwide, with the last products sold in August. This decision aligns with CEO Greg Foran's stance against suppliers' price increases amid inflation. Kroger will continue to sell other energy drink brands and plans to expand its house brands if vendors' prices are not acceptable.

Title: Beginning on Sept. 21, 2026, Kraft Heinz Company will sell the Capri Sun Big Pouch exclusively at Walmart.com for $6. The limited-edition release will run through Sept. 24, 2026.
Summary: Kraft Heinz Company will be selling a limited-edition Capri Sun Big Pouch exclusively on Walmart.com starting September 21, 2026, for $6. This special release will only be available for a short period, concluding on September 24, 2026.

Title: Pasta sold at Walmart stores nationwide recalled because of Listeria
Summary: Gias Foods has initiated a nationwide recall of two lots of bettergoods Authentic Italian Lemon Alfredo Fettuccine sold at Walmart due to potential Listeria monocytogenes contamination. The recalled frozen pasta is in 22-ounce yellow plastic packages and was identified through routine sampling by state agriculture departments. No illnesses have been reported, but consumers who have purchased the product are advised to monitor for Listeria symptoms.

Title: Element Brings New Smart TVs Powered by TiVo to Major U.S. Retailers
Summary: Element and TiVo have partnered to release new Element smart TVs powered by TiVo OS, now available at major U.S. retailers like Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and Target. These 4K Ultra HD televisions, offered in 50-inch and 65-inch sizes, aim to simplify entertainment discovery with a content-first platform. The collaboration expands TiVo OS's reach in the U.S. market, offering consumers an intuitive and affordable smart TV experience.

Title: ADT Blu Adds Walmart.com as Retail Channel for DIY Security
Summary: ADT Blu, the self-installed home security system, is now available on Walmart.com, expanding its retail presence. This move aims to make DIY security more accessible to consumers, offering flexible monitoring options including 24/7 professional monitoring or self-monitoring, without requiring a long-term contract or professional installation. ADT plans to continue expanding its DIY product line through additional retail channels.

Title: 7 Walmart recalls to check for, with about 60 stores across NJ
Summary: Walmart has issued recalls for seven products available in its New Jersey stores, ranging from food items to children's toys and household appliances. Consumers are advised to check their purchases against this list for potential safety hazards like listeria contamination, choking risks, or fire concerns. Most recalled items are eligible for a refund or replacement without a receipt.

Title: Uncrustables is a $1 billion brand. Now everyone wants in
Summary: J.M. Smucker's Uncrustables brand has become a $1 billion success, appealing to both kids and adults, including professional athletes. Its popularity has led to new competitors like Trader Joe’s, Welch’s, and Jams entering the frozen PB&J market, capitalizing on consumer nostalgia and convenience. Smucker is expanding Uncrustables' offerings and actively defending its market position through legal actions against similar products.

Title: Fort Worth aims to secure $433.8M Carrier Global Corporation plant
Summary: The city of Fort Worth is competing to attract a new $433.8 million manufacturing plant from Carrier Global Corporation, offering a seven-year tax abatement and nominating the project for a Texas Enterprise Zone designation. The plant would create 495 jobs with an average salary of $75,000 and would be the largest facility investment in Carrier's history. Fort Worth is up against three other states, two of which have lower property taxes.

Title: Costco now offers nationwide delivery on Uber and DoorDash
Summary: Costco has significantly expanded its e-commerce reach by launching nationwide delivery through partnerships with Uber Eats and DoorDash. This expansion builds on existing collaborations and addresses growing customer demand for same-day delivery, a segment that Costco's CEO noted is outperforming its overall digital business. Shoppers can now access nearly all U.S. Costco locations via Uber Eats and 630 locations across 47 states and D.C. through DoorDash, offering both on-demand and scheduled delivery options.

Title: Kroger yanks Red Bull nationwide as energy drink’s premium price comes under fire
Summary: Kroger has removed Red Bull from its shelves nationwide due to disagreements over pricing, as the grocery chain takes a tougher stance against supplier price hikes. This move comes amid rising consumer complaints about Red Bull's premium cost compared to other energy drinks, with some shoppers indicating they will switch brands or stores. The situation highlights a gamble for both Kroger and Red Bull as the standoff continues.

Title: How Big A Swing In eBay Stock Are You Actually Holding?
Summary: eBay stock is trading at $113, with a 28.7% return over the past year. The options market indicates a significant potential price swing for eBay, with a one-standard-deviation range between $79.44 and $160.45 over the next year. This implies a possible 29.6% downside or 42.1% upside, despite the acquisition of Depop and the growth of eBay Live, which will impact future operating income.

Title: Dillard’s to transfer listings to the Texas Stock Exchange
Summary: Dillard's Inc., a Little Rock-based retailer, is transferring its stock listings from the New York Stock Exchange to the new Texas Stock Exchange, following Walmart's recent move to Nasdaq. This decision comes after shareholders voted to re-domicile the company from Delaware to Texas, offering Dillard's certain protections from shareholder actions and a more prominent position on the new exchange. The move also aligns with Dillard's strong retail presence in Texas, its largest market.

Title: Colleen Lindholz Retires From Kroger
Summary: Colleen Lindholz, president of Kroger Health, has announced her retirement after 31 years with The Kroger Co. She was instrumental in developing Kroger's food-as-medicine strategy and co-founded Nourishing Change, an initiative to foster collaboration across various sectors for better health outcomes. Her departure follows other high-level executive retirements and she will deliver a keynote at the upcoming GLP-1 Shopper Summit.

Title: Amazon, Costco among companies fighting centralized tariff refund suits
Summary: Amazon, Costco, and over a dozen other companies are opposing a bid to centralize at least 25 lawsuits filed by customers seeking tariff refunds. The companies argue that centralizing the cases would not lead to efficiency gains because the specific details of each suit vary greatly, including pricing decisions and agreements, which are highly sensitive trade secrets. They contend that separate cases, some of which are nearing decisions, are more appropriate than a broad, cross-industry multidistrict litigation.

Title: Walmart Vs Kroger: Jim Cramer Couldn’t Figure Out Why Only One’s Shares Went Up
Summary: Jim Cramer expressed confusion over why Walmart's shares rose despite negative earnings, while Kroger's stock did not react positively to its own earnings report. Both companies faced challenges, with Kroger cutting its full-year sales growth guide and Walmart experiencing its slowest comparable sales growth in five years, yet both saw strong advertising revenue. Walmart's higher forward P/E ratio and lower short interest, compared to Kroger, suggest differing investor perceptions despite similar underlying business challenges regarding consumer spending.

Title: Walmart launches Tap to Pay in all Hawaii stores | Business
Summary: Walmart has introduced its Tap to Pay contactless payment option in all nine of its stores across Hawaii. This new feature allows customers to make purchases using credit/debit cards, phones, or smartwatches, aiming to streamline the checkout process. Hawaii is among the first 13 states to receive this rollout, with Walmart planning to expand Tap to Pay to all U.S. Walmart and Sam's Club locations by the end of 2026.

Title: Dollar Tree shares key update on higher prices
Summary: Dollar Tree has confirmed that its multi-price strategy, which includes items up to $7, is permanent and not a temporary measure against inflation. This shift follows strong Q2 2026 earnings, with total sales growth of 7.0% driven by customers purchasing higher-priced items. The company views multi-pricing as a key driver for growth and increased profitability, despite moving away from its original $1 price point.

Title: Did CareCredit Dental Booking Deal Just Shift Synchrony Financial's (SYF) Investment Narrative?
Summary: Synchrony Financial (SYF) has partnered with Intelibly Inc. to embed its CareCredit offering directly into Intelibly's dental appointment platform, allowing patients to access financing earlier in their treatment journey. This integration aligns with Synchrony's digital payment strategy and could influence loan receivables and health and wellness portfolio utilization. While it supports the company's broader digital push, the deal is unlikely to drastically alter Synchrony's investment narrative, which currently anticipates revenue growth but a decline in profits, focusing instead on credit quality and expense control.

Title: Frozen fettuccine sold at Walmart recalled over possible Listeria contamination
Summary: Gias Foods Inc. has issued a recall for two lots of bettergoods Authentic Italian Lemon Alfredo Fettuccine sold at Walmart stores nationwide due to potential Listeria monocytogenes contamination. The affected frozen 22-ounce packages have specific UPCs, lot numbers, and expiration dates. Listeria can cause severe and sometimes fatal infections, especially in vulnerable populations, and may lead to miscarriages or stillbirths in pregnant women.

Title: Should You Bet on the Businesses of Billionaires?
Summary: Bancreek Capital Advisors suggests investing in companies built by billionaires, even after their initial rapid growth, due to the unique advantages they possess. This strategy is embodied in their new Billionaires Club ETF (CLUB), which focuses on businesses with strong pricing power, scale, and durable moats, identified through a blend of fundamental value investing and data science. The ETF seeks steady, predictable compounding with low volatility, holding 30 equal-weighted names with global exposure.

Title: Coca-Cola accelerates US investments with $10 billion plan
Summary: The Coca-Cola Company and its bottling partners plan to invest $10 billion in U.S. infrastructure between 2026 and 2030, including new production, distribution, and office facilities. This investment builds on their existing network of over 70 production facilities and hundreds of distribution centers. The company also highlighted a study showing its system contributed $85 billion to the U.S. GDP in 2025, supported nearly 1 million jobs, and allocated $37 billion to U.S. suppliers.

Title: 2 men sentenced for stealing more than $350,000 in merchandise from Walmart stores in 11 states
Summary: Two men, Anthony Belser and George Mayo, have been sentenced for stealing over $350,000 in merchandise from Walmart stores across 11 states. Belser received a 25-year sentence with 10 years to be served in prison, while Mayo was sentenced to 40 years with 20 years in prison. The pair used a system of hiding merchandise in larger items to pay for lower-value boxes and have been ordered to pay $328,448 in restitution.

Title: Multi Price Gains Might Change The Case For Investing In Dollar Tree Stock (DLTR)
Summary: Dollar Tree's shift to a multi-price model, offering products at $3, $5, and up to $7, has shown positive early results with 7.0% sales growth and a 3.3% larger average ticket. This strategy aims to broaden the product range and improve store economics by appealing to value-focused shoppers while managing increased operational complexity. The article suggests that these multi-price gains could significantly impact Dollar Tree's long-term investment narrative, potentially leading to an 18% upside from its current price according to some analyses.

Title: Kroger Has More Leverage Over Premium Brands. Now Boar’s Head and Red Bull Are Losing Shelf Space
Summary: Kroger is removing premium brands like Boar’s Head and Red Bull from some of its stores as part of a new strategy to lower prices and gain leverage over suppliers. CEO Greg Foran aims to reinvest savings from more efficient operations and sourcing into making the retailer more affordable to compete with other major grocers. While Boar's Head confirmed its products are still available in many Kroger locations and other retailers, the move signals a shift in Kroger's merchandising strategy.

Title: 2 men sentenced for stealing more than $350,000 in merchandise from Walmart stores in 11 states
Summary: Two men, Anthony Belser (56) and George Mayo (52), have been sentenced for stealing over $350,000 worth of merchandise from Walmart stores across 11 states. Belser received a 25-year sentence with 10 years to be served in prison, while Mayo received a 40-year sentence with 20 years in prison. The thefts, which involved hiding high-value items in lower-value retail boxes, occurred over a 10-month period starting in August 2022.
